proposals.announcement_evidence: three expeditionary medical ships, an Expeditionary Fast Transport variant
proposals.rationale: The announcement itself states the three expeditionary medical ships are an Expeditionary Fast Transport variant, which is the index name and program title of SCN BLI 3043 verbatim. refute_a.reason: Fiscal 2023 and 2022 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds obligated and the lake shows 017-1611 on N00024-19-C-2227; construction of EPF-variant hulls on the EPF contract is the SCN EPF line's own work, not support for a platform it merely funds.

refute_b.reason: The announcement itself asserts the expeditionary medical ships are an Expeditionary Fast Transport variant, the index name matches exactly and has a single owner, and the index carries no separate medical-ship row that could claim the award instead.

proposals.announcement_evidence: This modification procures 10 F/A-18F Lot 46 aircraft, as well as two F/A-18F and five F/A-18E Lot 47 aircraft
proposals.rationale: Aircraft procurement: 17 F/A-18E and F airframes across Lots 46 and 47. The index row 'FA-18E/F' under BLI 0145 with lexicon_doc 330 (aircraft procurement) and program title 'F/A-18E/F (Fighter) Hornet' is the line that buys them; the announcement's designator differs only in slash placement. The other 0145 rows sit under lexicon_doc 338 and name bombs and fuzes, so the 330 row is the one this airframe buy belongs to.

refute_a.reason: Fiscal 2022 and 2023 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds are obligated and the lake shows 017-1506 on N00019-18-C-1046, matching the lexicon_doc 330 row's APN appropriation; 17 airframes are the line's product and the technical-data-package/sustainment rider is APN-funded and minority.

refute_b.reason: 'FA-18E/F' has one owner (0145/330); the F/A-18 names under 0204136N, 0505 and 0525 are improvement, modernization and sustainment rows, and the quoted evidence is the Lot 46/47 airframe buy, which none of them owns.

proposals.announcement_evidence: procurement of 15 F/A-18E and 3 F/A-18F Lot 42 full rate production aircraft for the Navy

refute_a.reason: Fiscal 2018 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds obligated in full for 18 full-rate-production airframes; the lake carries 017-1506 on N00019-17-C-0003, the APN account behind the doc-330 FA-18E/F row.

refute_b.reason: Eighteen Lot 42 full-rate-production airframes explicitly for the Navy; the aircraft-procurement name has a single index owner and the modernization/sustainment F/A-18 rows cannot claim a production airframe buy.

proposals.announcement_evidence: production and delivery of 22 F/A-18E and six F/A-18F Super Hornets in support of the government of Kuwait

This award buys 15 new-production airframes and their airborne electronic attack kits, a different scope from the modernization line, and the index carries no EA-18G airframe procurement row. proposals.announcement_evidence: four MQ-25A unmanned air vehicles
proposals.rationale: Design, development, fabrication, test, verification, certification and delivery of four MQ-25A air vehicles plus carrier air wing integration - engineering and manufacturing development, which belongs to RDT&E program element 0605414N (program title 'Unmanned Carrier Aviation (UCA)'), whose index name is 'MQ-25'. The same name is owned by aircraft procurement BLI 0449; that line buys production aircraft, which this 2018 development award is not. 'MQ-25A' differs from the index name only by the variant letter.

refute_a.reason: Fiscal 2018 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds are obligated and the lake shows only 017-1319 on N00019-18-C-1012 - PE 0605414N's own appropriation (lexicon_doc 340 = RDTEN_BA1-3_Book); EMD of four air vehicles is development work, and the APN alternative (BLI 0449) would need 1506N, which is absent from this award.

refute_b.reason: A true exact-name collision exists - 0449 owns the bare name 'MQ-25' on the aircraft-procurement side - but the record's own verbs resolve it: design, development, fabrication, test, verification and certification of four EMD air vehicles with carrier air wing integration to reach initial operational capability is the development PE's work, not a production aircraft buy, and MQ-25A is the same system as the index's MQ-25.

proposals.announcement_evidence: production of 105 Lot 17 Joint Strike Fighter aircraft
proposals.rationale: Joint Strike Fighter is named verbatim, but two rows of this index own that exact name - BLI 0147 'Joint Strike Fighter CV' and BLI 0152 'JSF STOVL' - and the award is long lead material for 105 Lot 17 aircraft spread across the Air Force, Navy, Marine Corps, non-DoD participants and FMS customers. Neither Navy line can be said to own the action, and most of the aircraft are not Navy at all. Recorded as weak.

proposals.announcement_evidence: production and delivery of 56 F135-PW-100 propulsion systems for the Air Force
proposals.rationale: The only F135 name this index carries is 'F135 Engine Core Upgrade (ECU)', a development item inside the F-35 C2D2 RDT&E program element. This announcement buys production propulsion systems, overwhelmingly for the Air Force and for non-DoD participants and FMS customers, with NAVAIR acting only as the joint program office's contracting activity. Matching a production engine buy to an engine-upgrade development name is the §3 pattern of naming a different increment of a program the line does not fund, so this is rejected rather than linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: definitizes the production and delivery of 112 F135-PW-100 propulsion systems for the Air Force
proposals.rationale: Same rejection as record 11: the index's only F135 name is the Engine Core Upgrade development item under the F-35 C2D2 RDT&E PE, while this modification definitizes production propulsion systems for the Air Force, Marine Corps, Navy and FMS customers. Production airframe engines are not the ECU development effort the line funds - §3 different-increment pattern.

proposals.announcement_evidence: production of Low Rate Initial Production Lot 10 F135-PW-100 propulsion systems
proposals.rationale: Components, parts and materials for Lot 10 low-rate initial production F135 propulsion systems. The only F135 name in the index is the Engine Core Upgrade, a later development effort in the F-35 C2D2 RDT&E line; LRIP production hardware is a different increment and a different appropriation, so the candidate name is rejected.

proposals.announcement_evidence: procure F-135 propulsion system spare parts
proposals.rationale: A ceiling increase to buy F-135 propulsion system spare parts, modules, support equipment and depot lay-in material for the Air Force, Marine Corps, Navy, FMS customers and non-DoD participants. Spares and depot material are sustainment, not the Engine Core Upgrade development the only F135 index row names - both a different increment and a different appropriation family. Rejected.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Low Rate Initial Production Lot VIII F135 propulsion systems contract
proposals.rationale: Lot VIII low-rate initial production F135 propulsion systems, 19 of them for the Air Force and four for the Navy, six PW-600 for the Marine Corps plus partner and FMS engines. The index's sole F135 name is the Engine Core Upgrade development item in the F-35 C2D2 RDT&E line, which is not what a 2014 LRIP engine buy funds. Rejected.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Lot 14 production and delivery of 48 F135-PW-100 propulsion systems for the Air Force
proposals.rationale: Lot 14 production engines, funded in the announcement's own words with fiscal 2020 aircraft procurement (Air Force and Marine Corps) dollars - not Navy RDT&E, and not the Engine Core Upgrade development item that is the index's only F135 name. Rejected on the §3 different-increment pattern.
